However, Hamas rejected it, stating that they would not agree to any ceasefire that does not include a pullout of IDF troops. Several hours after Israel respected UN's call to continue the humanitarian ceasefire, Hamas began firing rockets which were intercepted by the Iron Dome. The IDF resumed attacks on military targets in Gaza in response. Later, Hamas requested another 24-hour ceasefire via the UN, but took responsibility for continuing attacks. As Israel continued the demolition of tunnels between Gaza and Israel, Egypt announced that they had destroyed 13 tunnels connecting Gaza to Egypt, bringing the total number of tunnels destroyed on the Egyptian border to 1,639. The IDF announced that Ismail Muhammad Saad Akluk, a senior Hamas member who had been involved in Hamas' weapons development and research programs was killed when the Israeli Air Force bombed his vehicle. Israel's Health Ministry offered humanitarian aid which included medical equipment and blood donations worth millions of shekels to the Gaza Strip, which the Palestinian Authority refused. The IDF later announced that they had concluded their investigation into the UNRWA deaths. They stated that one mortar bomb had landed in a courtyard of the school but caused no injuries, and that the damage that caused casualties was not caused by the IDF. The UN stated that they will be conducting their own investigation. That afternoon, Israel announced for the second time in three weeks that a car bombing had been thwarted. In the evening, Barack Obama called Netanyahu and reaffirmed his support for Israel's right to defend itself against rockets and tunnels, but expressed concern about the civilian death toll in Gaza. He called for a disarmed and demilitarized Gaza in any ceasefire proposal. Hamas has said they will take the life of anyone who attempts to take their weapons.

records.text: Despite the unified Palestinian government, Fatah spoke out during the night against Hamas and their recent arrests of Fatah members within Gaza. At 07:00, the UN Security Council held an emergency meeting to issue a statement calling for both sides to have an immediate and indefinite humanitarian ceasefire. The statement did not mention Hamas or Israel, instead only referencing the Gaza conflict and requesting that Egypt mediate. In the afternoon, there were reports of an explosion at the Al-Shifa Hospital that resulted in dozens of injuries. Initial reports from Gaza stated the Israeli F-16 planes fired missiles at the hospital, but Israel stated that they believed the explosion was caused when militants attempted to fire a Fajr-5 rocket at Tel Aviv and it malfunctioned and exploded. Hamas stated that neither they nor the PIJ had anything to do with the explosion. In the evening, several Hamas members came out of a tunnel into Israel, with the intent to kidnap IDF soldiers, and engaged IDF forces. According to the IDF, five soldiers and at least one of the infiltrators were killed, and the rest of the infiltrators withdrew. The infiltrators attempted unsuccessfully to take an IDF soldier's body back with them. Hamas claimed that the infiltrators killed 10 IDF soldiers and all returned safely. In a separate incident, four IDF soldiers were killed by Hamas mortar fire toward Israel's Eshkol region. Shortly afterward, the IDF warned via text messages and phone calls the residents of Jabalia, Zeitoun and Shejaiya to evacuate. Soon after, Zeitoun and Jabalia came under fire. The evacuation warnings were later extended to Beit Hanoun and Beit Lahiya. In Gaza, an Israeli soldier was killed when an RPG hit his armored bulldozer. The militants responsible withdrew into a nearby building that was soon demolished by an IDF bulldozer, leaving eight militants dead, while two were found alive and taken prisoner. Hamas said that its fighters managed to kill 19 Israeli soldiers in three separate attacks. Israel criticized John Kerry's proposed ceasefire, saying it favors Hamas and its continuity. Furthermore, Israel informed other nations that no ceasefire deal will be accepted without the destruction of the tunnels leading from Gaza to Israel and the demilitarization of the Gaza Strip.

records.text: Shortly after midnight, France announced that they had agreed to transfer 8 million Euros to Gaza in aid. Israel targeted 70 locations within Gaza, including the home of senior Hamas political leader Ismail Haniyeh. Additionally, Israeli forces targeted the building containing Hamas' media offices for Al-Aqsa TV and radio. The PIJ announced that Rafah commander Ahmed Najam Abu Hamda was one of 32 killed by Israel. Fuel tanks located outside the only Gazan power plant were also struck, causing massive blackouts across Gaza overnight. In the afternoon, the PLO said that a 3-day unilateral ceasefire would be announced shortly, but Hamas rejected it. Later in the evening, it was unofficially announced that all sides had agreed to a ceasefire. Waddah Abu Amer, a political leader of the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine, his wife, and five children were killed in their home in Khan Younis by an army missile. In the early evening, five Palestinians emerged from a tunnel and were killed by the IDF. The militants were carrying a large number of explosives and weapons for a purported suicide mission. As of today, 200,000 of Gaza's 1.6 million residents are seeking shelter in UNRWA schools. 1,190 Palestinians have been killed through 22 days of the conflict. For the third time during the operation, the UNRWA found rockets stored in one of their schools, which was not being used as a shelter.

Hamas has in response been firing a greater number of rockets into Israel again, leading to the launch of Israel's Operation Protective Edge earlier this month as a countermeasure, all of which has contributed to an escalation towards a previously seen pattern of attack, retaliation, international mediation, ceasefire, broken ceasefire, and the resumption of violence. Yesterday, the Turkish Humanitarian Relief Foundation announced a new attempt to breach the Israeli naval blockade of Gaza. As talks in Cairo continued, reports suggested progress was being made towards a long-term ceasefire, albeit with Israel still not agreeing to building a seaport or an airport in Gaza. Hamas claimed that the Israeli Navy violated the ceasefire and fired at Gaza. Israel has maintained that a fishing boat attempted to leave the permitted fishing zone, leading to Navy warning shots.

records.label: Gaza conflict
records.text: Despite the ceasefire still being in effect, Netanyahu ordered the IDF to retaliate for the rocket fire. Israel struck four targets in Gaza. records.label: Gaza conflict
records.text: Overnight, news leaked that the US and Israel came to an agreement over the blockade of Gaza. Israel agreed to ease the blockade and in return the US will use their international influence to prevent Hamas from rearming. In the afternoon, three rockets fired from Gaza exploded outside of Be'er Sheva, breaking the ceasefire with the first action by either side in nearly 6 days. Shortly prior to this, Hamas spokesman Fawzi Barhoum stated "If Netanyahu doesn’t understand the language of politics in Cairo, we know how to make him understand," possibly hinting at the rocket fire, although Hamas denied involvement. Netanyahu ordered the IDF to retaliate against the renewed fire, and ordered the negotiators to return from Cairo. Later, the Iron Dome intercepted two rockets over Netivot. Two more rockets were shot down over Sderot and another two over Be'er Sheva, as well as several fired at Tel Aviv, which Hamas took credit for. Hamas announced that they blame Israel for the ending of the ceasefire. However, the US said they hold Hamas responsible and reiterated Israel's right to defend itself. According to a senior Fatah official, Qatar threatened Hamas' political bureau chief Khaled Mashal that it would expel him if Hamas accepted the Egyptian ceasefire deal.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: Haiti's worst earthquake in two centuries struck at 16:53 local time. Its epicentre was 15km south-west of Port-au-Prince, and it was quickly followed by two strong aftershocks of 5.9 and 5.5 magnitude. Phone lines to the country failed shortly afterwards, and the UN reported its local HQ had "sustained serious damage along with other UN installations'' and that "a large number'' of personnel were missing.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: As dawn broke, the extent of the damage and number of casualties started to become clearer, with the Red Cross indicating up to three million people had been affected, and Prime Minister Jean-Max Bellerive saying he believed more than 100,000 people had died. The cost of the damage could run into billions of dollars, with President Rene Preval reporting the collapse of multiple buildings in the country's capital. US President Barack Obama vowed "unwavering support" for Haiti following the "cruel and incomprehensible" disaster. UN officials reported that at least 14 people died when the UN's five-storey headquarters and two smaller buildings in Port-au-Prince collapsed. Around 100 were still thought to be missing.
records.background: On 12th January, 2010, Haiti suffered its worst earthquake in two centuries at 16:53 local time. The epicentre was 15km south-west of capital city Port-au-Prince, and it was quickly followed by two strong aftershocks of 5.9 and 5.5 magnitude.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: The search effort for earthquake survivors under the rubble were hampered by the lack of heavy-lifting equipment. The first US aid planes landed and US naval ships were on the way. EU states, Russia, and China were among those sending rescue and medical teams, and pledges of aid were made by countries around Latin America. The BBC's Andy Gallacher reported that in the capital Port-au-Prince there was no sense of a co-ordinated rescue effort, scant medical supplies and aid only trickling in. UN officials said mission head Hedi Annabi of Tunisia was among the up to 150 people missing from its 9,000-strong peacekeeping mission.\n
records.background: On 12th January, 2010, Haiti suffered its worst earthquake in two centuries. The epicentre was 15km from capital city Port-au-Prince. US President Barack Obama has vowed "unwavering support" for Haiti, calling the earthquake a "cruel and incomprehensible" disaster. Prime Minister Jean-Max Bellerive has estimated that more than 100,000 people have died.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: Many spent another day without food and shelter in Port-au-Prince, with survivors said to be dying in huge numbers, and clean water, food and medical supplies desperately needed. Bottlenecks and infrastructure damage were said to be holding up aid efforts. Time magazine photographer Shaul Schwarz said he had seen a roadblock formed with bodies of victims that he believed was "an act of anger'' by people not getting help. Estimates of the number of dead are put at as many as 50,000. UK firefighters rescued two-year-old Haitian girl Mia from the rubble of a collapsed kindergarten. UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon said one UN staff member, Estonian protection officer Tarmo Joveer, was found alive beneath the rubble of the international body's collapsed headquarters.
records.background: The epicentre for the earthquake in Haiti on January 12th was close to capital city Port-au-Prince. Assessment of damage and loss of life and the search for survivors is underway. The US, Russia, China, EU states and countries in Latin America have pledged aid, including rescue and medical teams.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: There were reports of gangs preying on residents and looting, and officials said thousands of prisoners were unaccounted for after the main prison was destroyed, contributing to rising fears over security. Damage to transport infrastructure still hindered the aid effort in a disaster a UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs spokesperson said was "like no other" in memory because the country had been "decapitated". Interior Minister Paul Antoine Bien-Aime estimated the total number of dead could be "between 100,000 and 200,000". The UN launched an appeal for $562m to help three million people for six months.
records.background: Damage to infrastructure from the earthquake near Port-au-Prince in Haiti on 12th of January has restricted access to shelter, clean water, food and medical supplies. Time magazine reported a roadblock was formed with bodies of quake victims as a potential “act of anger”.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: Reports from the epicentre of Tuesday's earthquake suggested the damage was even more dramatic than in the capital, with thousands left homeless and according to the UN up to 90% of buildings in Leogane destroyed. Rescuers pulled a woman alive from the rubble of a luxury hotel in what her husband, Reinhard Riedl, described to the Associated Press as "a little miracle" . The estimated death toll continues to rise. Speaking in Haiti, US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton said the US would be "here today, tomorrow and for the time ahead", asserting that "Haiti can come back even better and stronger in the future".
records.background: On 12th January, 2010, Haiti suffered its worst earthquake in two centuries. The epicentre was 15km from capital city Port-au-Prince. The US, Russia, China, EU states and countries in Latin America have pledged aid, including rescue and medical teams, but damage to infrastructure has slowed the effort.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: The leading US general in Haiti Lt Gen Ken Keen said it was a "reasonable assumption'' that up to 200,000 people might have died in last Tuesday's earthquake. Amidst reports of clashes with looters in the capital and crowds gathering at the gates of the airport, UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon said he would recommend that the Security Council boost UN troop numbers in Haiti by 2,000 for six months, and UN police numbers by 1,500. Former American President Bill Clinton, in Haiti as a special UN representative, said that given the circumstances, it was understandable that there had been some disorder. \nThousands of people were fleeing the capital in the hope of finding food and water.\n
records.background: Damage to infrastructure from the earthquake near Port-au-Prince in Haiti on 12th of January has restricted access to shelter, clean water, food and medical supplies. Security fears have increased as gangs have begun looting and preying on residents. After the main prison was destroyed by the earthquake, thousands of prisoners were missing.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: Scores of US troops arrived at the ruins of the presidential palace and the UN Security Council also voted unanimously to send a further 3,500 UN troops and police to Haiti. The BBC's Christian Fraser spoke of supplies running low and becoming increasingly expensive. Meanwhile, doctors said they were having to carry out hundreds of amputations, with only basic medical equipment, because of the large numbers of people suffering gangrene or traumatic injuries. Medecins Sans Frontieres reported that their plane carrying 12 tonnes of medical aid was repeatedly denied permission to land at Port-au-Prince's congested airport. So far 90 people have been found alive in Haiti's ruins.
records.background: Damage to infrastructure from the earthquake near Port-au-Prince in Haiti on 12th of January has restricted access to shelter and clean water and transport of aid from the airport. With a predicted death toll of up to 200,000 and mounting security concerns, the UN recommended a boost in UN troop numbers by 2,000 for six months, and UN police numbers by 1,500.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: A strong 6.1 magnitude aftershock rocked Haiti west of Port-au-Prince at 06:03 local time, causing already weakened buildings to collapse, as people were still being found alive in the rubble from the original quake. They included a five-year-old boy reportedly pulled from the ruins of his home by his uncle. More than 120 people altogether have been rescued by international teams. The US announced it was sending another 4,000 sailors and marines to Haiti for the earthquake relief effort. Victims unable to find treatment in Haiti have crossed the border into the Dominican Republic, but hospital are struggling to cope with the volume of patients. Haitian officials said 75,000 bodies had already been buried in mass graves. An estimated 1.5 million are homeless.
records.background: On 12th January, 2010, Haiti suffered its worst earthquake in two centuries. The epicentre was 15km from capital city Port-au-Prince. The US, Russia, China, EU states and countries in Latin America have pledged aid and contributed to the rescue and relief amidst estimations of up to 200,000 dead and thousands homeless.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: About 400,000 survivors will be moved to tented villages outside the capital, Port-au-Prince, Interior Minister Paul Antoine Bien-Aime announced. The International Organisation for Migration warned that more permanent shelter would soon be needed by the 500,000 people living outdoors. In a bid to deliver greater quantities of aid, the US military was operating at two airports in Haiti plus two in neighbouring Dominican Republic. The US Coast Guard partially reopened the capital's previously damaged main sea port.
records.background: With 75,000 victims' bodies already buried and an estimated 1.5 million left homeless from the original quake, a 6.1 magnitude aftershock further rocked Haiti west of Port-au-Prince at 06:03 local time. More US troops have been sent to help as the aid effort continues, with the BBC 's Gary Duffy saying the volume of patients is so great the hospitals in the Dominican Republic where desperate Haitians have sought treatment are struggling to cope.

records.label: Haitian earthquake
records.text: International search teams continued their work to find survivors, despite the Haitian government calling an official end to the rescue phase, and were rewarded by pulling Wismond Exantus from the remains of the Napoli Inn Hotel 11 days after the quake. Meanwhile, organisers of the Hope for Haiti telethon in the US said it had raised more than $57m for victims, a new record for disaster relief telethons.
records.background: With 75,000 victims' bodies already buried and an estimated 1.5 million left homeless as a result of the original earthquake on 12th January near capital city Port-au-Prince and a strong aftershock three days ago, a coalition of countries are continuing to provide aid, rescue and relief efforts in Haiti.

records.background: The Iraq War began on March 20th, 2003, when a United States-led coalition invaded Iraq and removed the government of Saddam Hussein with the stated rationale that Iraq has a weapons of mass destruction program and poses a threat to the US and its allies. Iraqi forces were quickly overwhelmed as coalition forces swept through the country, but an insurgency has emerged to oppose the coalition forces and the post-invasion Iraqi government, resulting in continuing political turmoil and armed conflict. Detainee abuse scandals have undermined the standing of US and British armed forces, while daily violence has left thousands dead and wounded, and stymied attempts to move the country forward. UN-mandated Operation Odyssey Dawn has begun with French fighter jets and US and British warships firing more than 110 cruise missiles against Libyan air defenses. US Vice Admiral William Gortney at a Pentagon briefing has said the operation is meant "to deny the Libyan regime from using force against its own people". Speaking on Libyan state TV, Gaddafi has argued that the UN charter provides for Libya's right to defend itself in a "war zone", saying weapons depots will be opened, and asking that "all you people of the Islamic nations and Africa, and Latin America and Asia, stand with the Libyan people in its fight against this aggression".

records.label: Libyan war
records.text: On the back of allied airstrikes, rebels retake Ajdabiya.\nEman al-Obeidy, a Libyan woman with bruises all over her body, bursts into a Tripoli hotel and tells international journalists how she was taken from a checkpoint and held for two days while 15 of Gaddafi's men beat and raped her. Government officials and hotel staff usher her outside to a car and drive her away. Government officials say she is mentally ill and drunk and call her a prostitute, but in a turnaround later say the accusations will be investigated. The suspects, in turn, file counter-charges for slander.

records.background: The Obama administration is planning an overhaul of the NSA's bulk phone records surveillance program amidst alleged agency overreach. The president has denied that federal agencies knew about a security flaw potentially compromising Internet users' passwords and other sensitive information.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Revelations that the United States has collected huge amounts of data about German citizens leaves Germany feeling the established rules of 21st century have been broken.
records.background: The Obama administration is planning an overhaul of the NSA's bulk phone records surveillance program amidst alleged agency overreach at home and abroad. Classified documents released by former NSA contractor Edward Snowden show the government agency infiltrated the servers of Chinese company Huawei.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Newly declassified documents show that Federal District Court Judge Rosemary Collyer rejected a major telephone provider's request to have Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court reconsider its approval of the NSA's bulk phone-records collection, upholding an earlier ruling that the Fourth Amendment offers no protections for metadata.
records.background: The Obama administration is planning an overhaul of the NSA's bulk phone records surveillance program amidst releases of documents, most notably by former NSA contractor Edward Snowden, supporting allegations of the security agency's overreach at home and abroad.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Plea deal negotiations between defense lawyer Plato Cacheris and federal prosecutors over Edward Snowden's release of classified data appear bogged down.\nCybersecurity coordinator Michael Daniel publishes on the White House website a series of questions it asks in deciding when to make public the discovery of major flaws in computer security. It appears to be distilled from more detailed guidance given to the NSA, FBI and others who often exploit flaws in Internet security.
records.background: Former National Security Agency contractor Edward Snowden released classified documents detailing the agency's surveillance activities. Former President Jimmy Carter has said while he's not certain, he would consider pardoning Snowden. President Obama has decided that the NSA should reveal most major Internet security flaws it discovers.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: After it was disclosed that National Security Agency was taping Chancellor Angela Merkel’s cellphone, German officials say effort to remake intelligence relationship between United States and Germany has collapsed. There will be no broad intelligence sharing or 'no-spy' agreement in place for Merkel's upcoming White House visit.
records.background: The Obama administration is planning an overhaul of the NSA's bulk phone records surveillance program amidst alleged agency overreach. Revelations that the United States collected huge amounts of data about German citizens has elicited distrust from the European nation.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: As they seek to project a unified front against Russia’s aggression in Ukraine, a cordial but strained meeting between Angela Merkel and President Obama sees the German Chancellor emphasize her country's continued opposition to United States surveillance practices, saying it's too soon to return to 'business as usual' following NSA eavesdropping of her phone calls.\nThe data collection and surveillance of American citizens debate has shifted its focus from the NSA to practices of Silicon Valley companies and whether restrictions imposed on the agency will spill over to the tech industry.
records.background: Revelations that the United States collected huge amounts of data about German citizens and a disclosure that the NSA had taped Chancellor Angela Merkel's cellphone has caused a collapse in the intelligence relationship between the two nations ahead of Merkel's visit to the White House.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Senior members of House Judiciary and Intelligence committees agree on similar but rival bills that would restrict the NSA's ability to collect Americans’ phone call data in bulk. A compromise bill is expected to pass.
records.background: The government has been working on a proposal for the overhaul of the NSA's bulk phone records surveillance program so that obtaining individual records would be possible only where a judge determines that phone numbers are likely associated with terrorism. President Obama has publicly endorsed the plan.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: The House Intelligence Committee embraces Judiciary Committee bill replacing the NSA's program for collecting bulk phone calls records.
records.background: The government has been working on a proposal for the overhaul of the NSA's bulk phone records surveillance program. Senior members of House Judiciary and Intelligence committees agreed on similar but rival bills, with a compromise bill expected to pass.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Glenn Greenwald's book No Place to Hide: Edward Snowden, the NSA, and the US Surveillance State notes documents that reveal Susan Rice, then American United Nations ambassador, asked the NSA in 2010 for intelligence about Security Council members. Documents leaked by Snowden reveal a wider net of United States' spying on envoys.
records.background: Former National Security Agency contractor Edward Snowden released classified documents detailing the agency's surveillance activities. The government has been working on a bill intended to replace the NSA's program for collecting bulk phone calls records in the US. Other revelations of agency overreach at home and abroad have surfaced, notably the taping of German Chancellor Angela Merkel’s cellphone.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Democratic Senators Mark Udall and Ron Wyden accuse the Obama administration of seeking to 'ignore or justify' statements it made to the Supreme Court about warrantless surveillance by the NSA.
records.background: Former National Security Agency contractor Edward Snowden released classified documents detailing the agency's surveillance activities. Americans’ emails and phone calls are among communications the government has collected without a warrant.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Declassified documents from Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court show a telephone company raised questions in 2009 and 2010 about the legality of a then-secret NSA program collecting records of Americans' calling habits.
records.background: Releases of classified information show Americans’ emails and phone calls are among communications the National Security Agency has collected without a warrant. Democratic Senators Mark Udall and Ron Wyden have accused the Obama administration of seeking to 'ignore or justify' statements it made to the Supreme Court about warrantless surveillance.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: China uses examples of NSA spying on corporations globally to argue that in indicting members of the People's Liberation Army cyberwarfare unit the Obama administration is guilty of capitalistic hypocrisy. Officials insist the US never acts on behalf of American companies while not denying it spies to advance American economic advantage as part of broad national security strategy.\nLeaders of both parties in House of Representatives have changed USA Freedom Act, a bill restricting power of government to obtain Americans’ records in bulk.  Civil liberties groups argue the changes leave the door open for the NSA to obtain enormous volumes of records.
records.background: Documents provided by former NSA contractor Edward Snowden show that the agency was prying into the servers of Chinese telecommunications company Huawei while warning Americans about the security risks of using its products.  Amidst allegations of NSA overreach, senior members of the House Judiciary and Intelligence committees agreed on similar but rival bills intended to overhaul the agency's bulk phone records surveillance program in the US.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Critics say legislation passed by the House of Representatives to limit domestic spying program falls far short of promises made by lawmakers in the wake of revelations of former NSA contractor Edward Snowden and question Congress's seriousness about reining in what they see as the nation's runaway spies.
records.background: Amidst allegations of NSA overreach, leaders of both parties in House of Representatives have changed the USA Freedom Act, a bill restricting power of government to obtain Americans’ records in bulk.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Edward Snowden tells Brian Williams of NBC News that he still considers himself to be an American patriot, attempting to justify leaking thousands of classified documents and explain accepting refuge from President Putin of Russia.
records.background: Former National Security Agency contractor Edward Snowden, with the help of journalists, released classified documents detailing the agency's surveillance activities, leading to increased scrutiny of the NSA's surveillance programs at home and abroad. Plea deal negotiations between Snowden's defense lawyer Plato Cacheris and federal prosecutors have stalled.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: The NSA releases what it says is the sole internal email from Edward Snowden before he fled the country with agency secrets, and insists the message undercuts the claim he protested the legality of surveillance programs before releasing documents to journalists.
records.background: Former National Security Agency contractor Edward Snowden released classified documents detailing the agency's surveillance activities. Plea deal negotiations between Snowden's defense lawyer Plato Cacheris and federal prosecutors have stalled. In an interview with Brian Williams of NBC News Snowden said that he still considers himself to be an American patriot.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: The NSA is harvesting huge numbers of images of people from communications that it intercepts through its global surveillance operations for use in sophisticated facial recognition programs, utilising new technology to exploit the flood of images included in communications.
records.background: Amidst allegations of NSA overreach, leaders of both parties in House of Representatives have changed the USA Freedom Act, a bill restricting power of government to obtain Americans’ records in bulk. Civil liberties groups argue the changes still leave the door open for the NSA to obtain enormous volumes of records.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Internet giants such as Google, Facebook and Microsoft are using new security protocols and increased encryption to prevent and render more expensive any attempts at the type of government surveillance exposed by Edward Snowden.
records.background: Former National Security Agency contractor Edward Snowden released classified documents showing the government agency had infiltrated the servers of Chinese telecommunications company Huawei. President Obama has decided that the NSA should reveal most major Internet security flaws it discovers, but a loophole could allow the agency to crack encryption on the Internet and to design cyberweapons.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Vice President Joe Biden Jr arrives in Brazil for meeting with President Dilma Rousseff, seeking an opening during the World Cup soccer tournament to thaw relations with the country, which soured after revelations of the NSA's surveillance practices.
records.background: Former National Security Agency contractor Edward Snowden released classified documents detailing the agency's surveillance activities in the US and abroad. China has accused the Obama administration of capitalistic hypocrisy, while Germany's relationship with the US has been strained by revelations of the NSA gathering data from German citizens and taping Chancellor Angela Merkel's cellphone.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: The House of Representatives votes to bar the NSA from looking for Americans’ communications without a warrant within emails and phone calls gathered while targeting foreigners.
records.background: Amidst allegations of NSA overreach, leaders of both parties in House of Representatives have supported changes to the USA Freedom Act, a bill aimed at restricting power of government to obtain Americans’ records in bulk.

records.label: NSA leak
records.text: Newly installed NSA director Admiral Michael Rogers says the crisis resulting from Edward Snowden's document leak, while serious, is nevertheless manageable, detailing a series of steps being taken by the agency to prevent a similar future leak while warning that it's impossible to fully safeguard against intrusion by a dedicated insider.
records.background: Former National Security Agency contractor Edward Snowden released classified documents showing the government agency had infiltrated the servers of Chinese telecommunications company Huawei, leading to further revelations of clandestine espionage and data gathering by the NSA at home and abroad.

records.text: A woman in Mexico's Oaxaca state, later crucial to piecing together the epidemic, becomes ill.

records.text: A 39-year-old woman infected with swine flu dies of severe viral pneumonia in San Luis Potosi, central Mexico.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: In Oaxaca state, a woman with flu-like symptoms dies.
records.background: Mexican health authorities begin picking up outbreaks of a flu-like illness, including a woman who falls ill in Oaxaca state. A 39-year-old woman dies of swine flu in San Luis Potosi.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: The Pan-American Health Organization, part of the WHO, receives notification from the Mexican health department of its swine flu outbreak.
records.background: Mexican health authorities begin picking up outbreaks of flu-like illnesses. A 39-year-old woman later dies of swine flu in San Luis Potosi while a woman in Oaxaca dies suffering flu-like symptoms.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: The World Health Organization notifies Mexico of strange flu cases occurring in California.
records.background: Mexican health authorities alert the Pan-American Health Organization about a swine flu outbreak following picking up outbreaks of a flu-like illness and the deaths of two Mexican women.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: A teleconference by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention enables Mexico and WHO to discuss the situations in California and Oaxaca.
records.background: Mexican health authorities alert the Pan-American Health Organization about a swine flu outbreak following the deaths of two Mexican women. The WHO notifies Mexico of strange flu cases in California.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: The US confirms two children, a 10-year-old boy and a nine-year-old girl, who live in adjacent California counties around 210km apart, have tested positive for what the CDC has identified as a new type of swine flu.
records.background: Mexican health authorities alert the Pan-American Health Organization about a swine flu outbreak following the deaths of two Mexican women. The WHO notifies Mexico of strange flu cases in California and discussions are had via a CDC teleconference.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: The Mexican Health ministry issues a nationwide alert following the death of 20 people countrywide from flu-like illness this year. \nTests on Mexican samples in Canada confirm that those cases feature the same strain as the Californian outbreak.
records.background: Mexican health authorities alert the Pan-American Health Organization and make contact with the WHO and CDC in the US after a swine flu outbreak kills two. The CDC reports a new type of swine flu is the illness identified in two children in California.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: Another seven US cases are identified: five in southern California and two in a town near San Antonio, Texas.\nAs the flu spreads, Mexico closes schools in Mexico City and the surrounding area. A Canadian laboratory IDs the new virus, which is appearing outside of Oaxaca state.
records.background: Mexico makes contact with health authorities in the US following a swine flu outbreak is confirmed to have killed two people. The country reports 20 people have died from flu-like illness this year and issues a nationwide alert. Two children in California test positive for swine flu. Tests performed in Canada show Mexico and California cases feature the same strain.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: Mexico has identified more than 900 suspected cases and 62 deaths linked to swine flu, including 854 cases of pneumonia in Mexico City, of which 59 have proved fatal. San Luis Potosi has 24 reported cases, with three deaths, while in Mexicali, near the US border, there have been four cases without fatality.\nThe CDC says Mexican patients had the same H1N1 virus as was found in the United States. \nThe WHO says it activated its command center for acute public health events.
records.background: Mexico makes contact with health authorities in the US following a swine flu outbreak is confirmed to have killed two people. Tests performed in Canada show cases in California feature the same strain of the virus as in Mexico, now also reported in Texas. As a preventative measure, Mexico City closes its schools.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: Mexican President Felipe Calderon issues an emergency decree affording government special powers to run tests on sick people and order them to be isolated as health officials report over 1,300 suspected cases and 81 deaths "probably linked to the virus". \nThe US Centres for Disease Control reports it has so far confirmed 11 cases of swine flu: seven in California, two in Texas and two in Kansas. There are also eight suspected cases in New York City after 200 students at a high school fell ill.\nMeanwhile, Northwick Park Hospital in north London reported negative tests for swine flu on a British Airways cabin crew.
records.background: Mexico confirms 900+ suspected swine flu-related cases and 62 deaths, predominantly in Mexico City. CDC tests show US and Mexican outbreaks are caused by the same H1N1 virus. Mexico City closes its schools and the WHO activates its acute public health events command center.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: New Zealand health minister Tony Ryall says 10 students who traveled to Mexico who tested positive for flu are "likely" to have swine flu.\nThe US declares a public health emergency while Canada confirms its first cases.
records.background: Mexico reports over 1,300 suspected swine flu cases and 81 deaths linked to the virus and issues an emergency decree to provide special powers for testing and isolating the sick. The CDC reports growing numbers of cases across four US states.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text:
The UK's first two cases of swine flu are confirmed. Newly-wed couple Iain and Dawn Askham, recently home from their honeymoon in Mexico, tested positive and were admitted to Monklands Hospital in Airdrie. Seven of their close family and friends are being treated after showing mild flu-like symptoms.
Spain's health minister Trinidad Jimenez confirms Europe's first cases. 
The World Health Organization's emergency committee raises the pandemic threat level for swine flu from phase three to four, indicating a significantly increased risk of a global outbreak of a serious new disease.
A 22-month-old Mexican boy dies from swine flu while visiting Texas. The U.S. State Department advises against non-essential travel to Mexico, whose death toll rises above 150.
records.background: Mexico reports over 1,300 suspected swine flu cases and 81 deaths linked to the virus and issues emergency decree to provide special powers for testing and isolating the sick. The CDC reports growing numbers of cases across four states and the US declares a public health emergency. First Canada cases demonstrates spread of the virus.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: Nearly 2,000 people in Mexico are believed to be infected with swine flu, while South Korea announces its first probable case. The number of confirmed cases among students at a school in New York school rises to 28, bringing the number of confirmed US cases to 42 in five states, doubling weekend reports. \nMajor travel agencies and tour operators cancel flights to Mexico and British holidaymakers are brought home as the Foreign Office advises against all but essential travel to the country and advises British citizens living in Mexico to "consider whether they should remain".\nIsrael and New Zealand confirm cases, and Scottish Health Secretary Nicola Sturgeon announced tests were being carried out on a total of 23 other people, including nine people who'd been in contact with confirmed cases Mr and Mrs Askham and subsequently experienced "mild" symptoms. The other 14 people were thought to have traveled in affected areas or had contact with someone who had.
records.background: Mexico issues emergency decree to provide special powers for testing and isolating amidst increasing swine flu cases. The WHO's emergency committee raises the pandemic threat level from three to four, reflecting the increase in suspected cases globally. Scottish newlyweds Iain and Dawn Askham who recently returned home from honeymooning in Mexico are confirmed as the first two UK swine flu cases. The US declares a public health emergency and the State Department advises against non-essential travel to Mexico.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text:
With only seven more suspected deaths, bringing the total to 159, the toll from the swine flu epidemic appears to be stabilising in Mexico. 2,500 others are possibly affected, though health secretary Jose Cordova says only 26 cases, including seven deaths, have been definitively confirmed as swine flu. 
Germany becomes the third European country to have the virus as it reports three cases. 
The number of confirmed cases in New Zealand rises to 14, while officials in Australia are testing more than 100 people with flu symptoms. In Malaysia one person is "under close observation", and the second case has been confirmed in Israel. Scotland has announced 24 new suspected cases are being investigated. Combined with new cases announced on Wednesday and pending results of those in contact with the previously confirmed cases Iain and Dawn Askham, this leaves a total of 32 cases under investigation in Scotland. 
WHO raises its pandemic alert to phase 5, meaning the world is at imminent risk of a pandemic. 
Mexico's president Felipe Calderón orders partial economic shutdown from May 1st.
records.background: Nearly 2,000 people in Mexico are believed to be infected with swine flu, while South Korea announces its first probable case amidst increasing suspected cases globally. The British Foreign Office and US State Department advise against non-essential travel to Mexico. The CDC reports growing numbers of cases across four states and the US declares a public health emergency. New cases are confirmed in Israel and New Zealand and the US confirms 42 cases across five states.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text:
Health Minister Nicola Sturgeon said 27 possible and one "probable" swine flu case, a contact of Scotland's only confirmed cases Iain and Dawn Askham, were under investigation. If confirmed this would be the first case of onward transmission in Scotland. 
24 of 32 suspected cases tested negative on Wednesday, but 19 new travel-related cases emerged by Thursday. 
Meanwhile, the Askhams have been released from hospital. 
A dedicated swine flu advice line for Scotland that will go live on Thursday afternoon has also been announced. It can be accessed through NHS 24 on 08454 24 24 24.
records.background: In Mexico around 2,500 people are believed to be infected and 159 dead from swine flu. South Korea, Israel, New Zealand, and Germany are among countries confirming cases. Scottish newlyweds Iain and Dawn Askham who recently returned home from honeymooning in Mexico were confirmed as the first two cases in the UK. The British Foreign Office and US State Department advise against non-essential travel to Mexico. The WHO raises the pandemic threat level from four to five.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: The US CDC says the swine flu outbreak may not be as severe as first thought.\nScottish Health Minister Nicola Sturgeon said another "probable" case was under investigation along with a further 19 new possible cases, all travel-related, bringing the total suspected cases under investigation to 29. With three confirmed Scottish cases and two more in England, the confirmed UK total stands at 15. Tests also confirm the first human-to-human transfer of swine flu in the UK, with Graeme Pacitti from Falkirk contracting it after contact with Iain and Dawn Askham, the couple who contracted the virus after honeymooning in Mexico. \nThe World Health Organization said it had no immediate plans to move its pandemic alert level from five to the highest level of six.

records.text: Mexico reports slowing of the swine flu virus.
records.background: In Mexico around 2,500 people are believed to be infected and 159 dead from swine flu. South Korea, Israel, New Zealand, and Germany are among countries confirming cases. Tests also confirm the first human-to-human transfer of swine flu in the UK. In the US, the CDC says the swine flu outbreak may not be as severe as first thought. The WHO leaves its pandemic alert at five rather than move to the highest level of six.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: Scotland confirms its fourth case of swine flu, a man from the Ayrshire and Arran health board area, thought to have picked up the virus in Texas without connection to previous cases. \nThe Scottish Government said first confirmed case, Iain Askham, had attended a concert in Edinburgh days after returning from Mexico. That he'd contracted the virus went unidentified at the time.
records.background: With thousands suspected of having been infected and 159 confirmed dead, Mexico reports a slowing of the swine flu virus in the country. The US CDC says the outbreak may not be as severe as first thought. Scottish newlyweds Iain and Dawn Askham who recently returned home from honeymooning in Mexico were confirmed as the first two cases in the UK, with the case total rising to 15. The WHO leaves its pandemic alert at five rather than move to the highest level of six.

records.label: Swine flu
records.text: Tests were taking place on a fifth "probable" and 19 possible swine flu cases in Scotland, as the number of confirmed UK cases rose by nine to 27. Health Secretary Nicola Sturgeon said Scotland was to send 1.45 million surgical face masks to England from its nine million stockpile to plug England and Wales's shortfall.\nMexico says business operations will return to normal on May 6th.
records.background: Mexico reports a slowing of the swine flu virus. The US CDC says the outbreak may not be as severe as first thought. The Scottish Government said the first confirmed UK case, Iain Askham, had attended a concert in Edinburgh days after returning from Mexico. Scotland's fourth confirmed case, a man from the Ayrshire and Arran health board area, is thought to have picked up the virus in Texas without connection to previous cases.

records.label: Ukraine conflict
records.text: On March 1st, 2014, the de facto Crimean Prime Minister Sergey Aksyonov takes what he calls temporary control of security in Crimea, ordering all commanders to obey or resign. The Ukrainian Navy and Ukrainian Sea Guard are reportedly forced to leave their bases in Sevastopol. Ukrainian journalists are prohibited from entering Crimea, reportedly on the orders of members of the Supreme Council. Aksyonov sets a March 30th date for a self-sovereignty referendum. He also appeals directly to Russian President Vladimir Putin, calling for Russia to "provide assistance in ensuring peace and tranquility on the territory" of Crimea. Demonstrations, which various Russian news media outlets start to label "Russian Spring", take place against the new authorities in Kiev and in support of Russians in Crimea occur throughout Eastern and Southern Ukraine. Thousands of people protest in Kharkiv, Melitopol, Yevpatoriaa, Odessa, and Mariupol, with reports of Ukrainian flags being replaced with the Russian tricolor at administration buildings. In Donetsk, as well as demonstrations, a new pro-Russian governor is elected. In Zaporizhia as many as 5,000 protesters gather to save the Lenin monument and rally against the Kiev government. The Russian Consulate in Simferopol start to issue Russian passports to residents of Ukraine. Members of the former Ukrainian riot police, Berkut, are among the first in Crimea to be granted Russian citizenship. The interim Ukrainian president, Oleksandr Turchynov, signs a decree declaring the appointment of Sergei Aksyonov as the head of the government of Crimea to be unconstitutional. Russian President Vladimir Putin formally asks the Federation Council for permission to "use the armed forces of the Russian Federation on the territory of Ukraine until the normalization of the socio-political situation in the that country." Hours later, they unanimously grant permission. According to Damon Wilson, vice president of the Atlantic Council, the United States Congress is "considering authorizing a defense arms package to Ukraine", as US president Barack Obama tells Putin to pull forces back to bases.

records.label: Ukraine conflict
records.text: In Zaporizhia, over 5,000 counter-protest against pro-Russian demonstrations and the Russian intervention. They also protest against people seizing state buildings and raising Russian flags. Similar rallies are held in Dnipropetrovsk, Odessa, Mykolaiv and Kharkiv, with some drawing as many as 10,000 people. Newly appointed chief of the Ukrainian Navy, Denis Berezovsky, announces on TV that he refuses to follow orders from the self-declared government in Kiev, declaring loyalty to Crimean authorities and people, and shortly after gets replaced by Serhiy Hayduk. A Ukrainian marine infantry detachment stationed around Feodosiya is surrounded by armed men demanding surrender. In Sudak, radar station personnel are forced to give up their arms. In Sevastopol, reports say the Ukrainian Navy building is under siege and land-based assault by the Russian Army. At a Ukrainian military base near the village of Perevalne, there is an ongoing standoff between a handful of Ukrainian marines loyal to Kiev and the surrounding Russian and Crimean forces. Interim President Oleksandr Turchynov orders all Ukrainian military reservists to be called up, as interim PM Yatsenyuk says Russia has effectively declared war.\nThe government of Crimea announces the formation of its own Defense Ministry and appoints as governors of eastern provinces powerful Ukrainian oligarchs who have thrown their weight behind the revolutionary government. In a ceremony in the Council of Ministers chamber in the presence of various regional government officials and mayors, the head of the Security Service of Crimea, Petyor Zima, Chief of Department of Internal Affairs in the Crimea, Sergey Abisov, the head of Service for Emergency Situations, Sergei Shakhov, and acting Chief of the Border Guards of Crimea, Victor Melnichenko, all take an oath of allegiance to the people of the so-called "Putin-backed" Crimea. \nThe US says Russia is in control of Crimea.
records.background: Earlier this year, pro-Russian Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych was ousted from office as a result of the pro-European Euromaidan uprising. Parliament adopted a bill to repeal the 2012 law which gave Russian language an official status, which though not enacted, provoked negative reactions in Russian-speaking regions, while the Russian media has stoked fears by suggesting that the country's ethnic Russian population is in imminent danger. Demonstrations by pro-Russian and anti-government groups have taken place in major cities across the eastern and southern regions of Ukraine. An interim government has been established and early presidential elections scheduled. Yesterday, the de facto Crimean Prime Minister Sergey Aksyonov took what he called temporary control of security in Crimea, ordering all commanders to obey or resign. The Ukrainian Navy and Ukrainian Sea Guard were reportedly forced to leave their bases in Sevastopol. Ukrainian journalists are now prohibited from entering Crimea. Aksyonov has set a March 30th date for a self-sovereignty referendum. He also appealed directly to Russian President Vladimir Putin for assistance. Putin formally asked the Federation Council for permission to "use the armed forces of the Russian Federation on the territory of Ukraine until the normalization of the socio-political situation in the that country", which they unanimously granted. The United States Congress is reportedly "considering authorizing a defense arms package to Ukraine", with US president Barack Obama telling Putin to pull forces back to bases.

records.label: Ukraine conflict
records.text:
Over 2,000 protesters waving Russian flags gather at Donetsk Oblast administrative building, break through police barricades and retake the facility. The pro-Russian group is led by Pavel Gubarev, a former member of the neo-Nazi "Russian National Unity" party, who claims to be the people's governor of the region.
Up to 500 demonstrators with Russian flags who oppose the new authorities in Kiev, attempt to seize the Odessa Regional State Administration building. They demand a referendum held on the establishment of an "Odessa Autonomous Republic". They break windows and enter the building and are met by Oblast chairman and Party of Regions official Mykola Leonidovych Skoryk, who tells the crowd the police could not allow such an "assault" and that Ukrainians "must live peacefully in a single state". Protesters call him a traitor.
Ukrainian troops stationed in Crimea are urged to surrender by March 3rd at 5 am or face an armed confrontation via an ultimatum issued by Alexander Vitko, the commander of the Russian Black Sea Fleet. This ultimatum is later denied by Russian officials. On the same day, Russian soldiers seize a Kerch Strait ferry terminal in the city of Kerch, the easternmost point of Crimea.
Crimea's State Television and Radio Transmitting Center forces the independent broadcaster Chernomorskaya Teleradiokompaniya off the air. The station, which has covered the political tension in the region, is one of two local broadcasters available to Crimean residents.
records.background: Earlier this year, pro-Russian Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych was ousted from office as a result of the pro-European Euromaidan uprising. An interim government has been established and early presidential elections scheduled. Demonstrations by pro-Russian and anti-government groups have taken place in major cities across the eastern and southern regions of Ukraine. De facto Crimean Prime Minister Sergey Aksyonov has taken control of security in Crimea, appealed to Vladimir Putin for assistance and received a pledge of military support from the Russian president. Yesterday, newly appointed chief of the Ukrainian Navy, Denis Berezovsky, announced on TV that he was refusing to follow orders from the self-declared government in Kiev, declaring loyalty to Crimean authorities and people, and was shortly after replaced by Serhiy Hayduk. Ukrainian armed forces and strategic buildings have been the subject of sieges, intimidation, and takeovers by Russian and Crimean forces. Interim President Oleksandr Turchynov has ordered all Ukrainian military reservists to be called up. Interim PM Yatsenyuk says Russia has effectively declared war. Meanwhile, the government of Crimea has announced the formation of its own Defense Ministry and appointed as governors of eastern provinces powerful Ukrainian oligarchs who have thrown their weight behind the revolutionary government. The US has said that Russia is now in control of Crimea.

records.label: Ukraine conflict
records.text: Pro-Russian separatists consolidate their control of the local Regional Administration in Donetsk. Pavel Gubarev is elected governor. He tells reporters "We don't want to give our money anymore to Kiev. We want more freedom for our city in a new federation or confederation that allows us to embrace the friendly ties and positive feelings towards us of the people of Russia". Allegations that many of the demonstrators have been bused in from Russia, specifically from the Rostov region, are levelled by opponents. A local journalist doesn't doubt many have been paid to participate but suggests most protesters are from within the city. There follows later a peaceful protest against the pro-Russian RSA occupiers and in support of a united Ukraine.\nPutin ends military exercises, pulling troops back from Ukrainian borders, saying that the soldiers occupying military bases were not Russian soldiers, but local forces of self-defense. He says for now there's no need to send forces into Ukraine, but that Russia reserves the right to use "all means" as a last resort to threats of anarchy.\nAround 200 unarmed Ukrainian soldiers of the 240th Tactical Air Brigade march towards Belbek Airbase, demanding their jobs back. The guarding pro-Russian forces fire warning shots in the air. After hours of negotiations, the pro-Russian forces agree to allow joint patrols of the base.

Demonstrations by pro-Russian and anti-government groups have taken place in major cities across the eastern and southern regions of Ukraine. De facto Crimean Prime Minister Sergey Aksyonov has taken control of Crimea with the backing of Russia. Ukrainian armed forces and strategic buildings have been the subject of sieges, intimidation, and takeovers by Russian, pro-Russian, and Crimean forces. Yesterday, over 2,000 protesters waving Russian flags took control of Donetsk Oblast administrative building. The pro-Russian group is being led by Pavel Gubarev, a former member of the neo-Nazi "Russian National Unity" party, who claims to be the people's governor of the region. A similar takeover of Odessa's Regional State Administration building also occurred. Meanwhile, Ukrainian troops stationed in Crimea were urged to surrender or face an armed confrontation via an ultimatum issued by Alexander Vitko, the commander of the Russian Black Sea Fleet. This ultimatum was later denied by Russian officials.

records.label: Ukraine conflict
records.text:
In Donetsk, a bomb threat forces the evacuation of the Regional Administration building, which forces out the occupying pro-Russian activists. The Ukrainian flag is briefly raised over the building, though hundreds of pro-Russian protesters retake the building in the evening and once again raise the Russian flag. However, up to 5,000 protest for unity in Ukraine and against Russian intervention, the largest of its kind in Donetsk since the unrest began. 1,000 pro-Russia counter-protesters attempt to confront the Ukrainian unionists, but the two are kept apart by police. Ukrainian unionists are also protected by FC Shakhtar Donetsk's fanatical "ultras". Meanwhile, 1,000 pro-Russian protesters march in Kharkiv, demanding a referendum on federalism for Ukraine and making Russian a state language. Police keep the demonstrators away from the Kharkiv Oblast RSA building, which continues to fly the Ukrainian flag.
The Crimean government announce that "more than 700 soldiers and officers" from the 50th, 55th and 147th anti-aircraft missile regiments, stationed in Yalta, Feodosia and Fiolente respectively, have defected to their side by "declaring their readiness to defend the population of Crimea". This is in addition to the 204th Fighter Unit of the Ukrainian Air Force, which defected on March 3rd. The Crimeans claim to have 6,000 defectors from the armed forces on their side.
Thirty-five Russian soldiers are said to have attacked the border checkpoint in Kerch. Meanwhile, the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine reports that Ukrainian Colonel General Mykhailo Koval has been taken hostage. One witness claims that he was taken by Russian bikers who attacked the personal car of Koval in Yalta.
In Simferopol, unknown gunmen take UN special envoy to Ukraine Robert Serry hostage. UN Deputy Secretary General Jan Eliasson clarifies Robert Serry had been threatened but had not kidnapped. Serry is expected to continue his work in Kiev due to the situation in Crimea.
The Shevchenko district court of Kiev, meanwhile, rules on the detention of the self-proclaimed leaders Sergey Aksyonov and Vladimir Konstantinov. The General Prosecutor of Ukraine opens criminal proceedings against the commander of Black Sea Fleet Aleksandr Vitko on the facts of incitement to treason and sabotage organization.
Three deputies of the Batkivshchyna party submit a bill in the Verkhovna Rada that would abolish the country's official neutrality and make Euro-Atlantic integration and NATO membership a foreign policy priority for Ukraine.
A wiretapped telephone conversation is leaked on YouTube of Estonian Foreign Minister Urmas Paet and EU foreign affairs chief Catherine Ashton discussing the issue of sniper-rifle fire during the 2014 Ukrainian revolution. Speaking about a doctor named Olga who was on the scene, Paet told Ashton, "The same Olga told that, well, all the evidence shows that people who were killed by snipers from both sides among policemen and then people from the street [sic]. So that there is now stronger and stronger understanding that behind the snipers it was not Yanukovych but it was somebody from the new coalition". The Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs later issues a statement confirming the tape's authenticity, but denying that "the new coalition" refers to the protesters who later overthrew Yanukovych and installed a new government in Kiev. The doctor referred to, Olga Bogomolets, speaks out to deny the claims, stating she only saw the protesters' wounds, and that the government assured her that an investigation would be opened.

records.label: Ukraine conflict
records.text:
The Supreme Council of Crimea vote to formally accede as part of the Russian Federation after 6 decades as part of the Ukrainian state. The Supreme Council's decision will be put to the Crimean people via referendum if the request is granted by Russia. The previously announced referendum is moved up to the 16th of March. The Ukrainian government immediately condemns the measure and argues that any unilateral referendum initiated by the current Crimean authorities would be unconstitutional, being joined in their condemnation by the US and EU. Refat Chubarov, leader of the Mejlis of the Crimean Tatar People, announces that deeming it illegitimate, they will not take part in the referendum. The Tatars report that their homes are marked with Xs by unidentified gangs.
Armed men seize the Simferopol Radio and Television Transmitting Station, and discontinue the broadcast of Kiev-based Channel 5 and 1+1 television channels, replacing their frequencies with the Moscow-based Rossiya 24 news channel.
Russian sailors scuttle the decommissioned cruiser Ochakov at the entrance to Donuzlav Bay in western Crimea as a blockship, in an attempt to prevent Ukrainian navy ships from gaining access to the Black Sea.
A mission of observers from the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe has been stopped from entering Ukraine's Crimean Peninsula by unidentified men in military fatigues for the third time.
After retaking the Donetsk RSA the previous day, pro-Russian protesters lose control of the building after a pre-dawn offensive led by police and the national Security Service of Ukraine. In addition to capturing control of the RSA and hoisting the Ukrainian flag, the SBU arrest self-proclaimed new Donetsk governor and pro-Russian protest leader Pavel Gubarev, along with about 70 of his supporters.

The Crimeans claim to have 6,000 defectors from the armed forces on their side.

Russia's state gas company Gazprom warns Kiev that its gas supply might be cut off.
Two Associated Press journalists from Bulgaria are beaten while taking photos outside the missile defense base A2355 outside the Crimean city of Sevastopol and their equipment is confiscated.

records.text:
Ukraine says an officer was killed as a military base was stormed in Simferopol, Crimea, the first such death in the region since pro-Russian forces took over in late February. It's later reported a pro-Russian solder has also died.
Crimean Deputy Prime Minister Rustam Temirgaliyev says in an interview with RIA Novosti the new government in Crimea wants to regularize the land unofficially taken over by Crimean Tatar squatters following the collapse of the Soviet Union. Russian President Vladimir Putin makes an address calling for the creation of "two new constituent entities within the Russian Federation: the Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol". Putin states that "Russia and Ukraine were not just neighbors but one nation" and that Russia would always "protect" the speakers of the Russian language in Ukraine. He says he sees the Yatsenyuk Government as "an illegitimate puppet government under the control of radicals". Putin also accuses nationalists, neo-Nazis, Russophobes and anti-Semites of being behind the "coup" in Ukraine.
Ukrainian Prime Minister Arseniy Yatsenyuk makes an address stating that his government has introduced "a special position of deputy prime minister in the government" tasked with "decentralization of the administration" "which will give the regions, cities, and districts broad powers and funding needed for the development of the regions". He also claims "Law enforcement agencies have collected compelling evidence of the involvement of Russian secret services in unrest in the east of our country".

records.background: Inspired by protests that helped oust Tunisia's president, in Yemen hundreds of protesters, including students, gathered at Sana'a University to call for an end to President Ali Abdullah Saleh's 32-year rule.

records.label: Yemen crisis
records.text: Yemen's ruling party calls for dialogue with the opposition. Saleh supporters counter Yemenis trying to march to the Egyptian embassy in Sana'a to express solidarity with Egyptian antigovernment demonstrators. The protesters chant "the people want the regime to fall".

records.background: Protesters are calling for an end to Yemeni President Saleh's 32-year rule. The president has promised reforms, saying he won't seek a new mandate when his term ends in 2013. records.label: Yemen crisis
records.text: Leaders of two of Yemen's most important tribes abandon the president.

records.label: Yemen crisis
records.text: In huge new protests near Sana'a University, tens of thousands of opposition activists demand removal of Saleh, who fires five of 22 provincial governors, some for criticizing the protest crackdowns.
records.background: Protesters are calling for an end to Yemeni President Saleh's 32-year rule. Saleh's supporters have been countering the protests. records.label: Yemen crisis
records.text: The opposition presents Saleh with a plan for a smooth transition of power, offering him a graceful exit. He proposes drawing up a new constitution to create a parliamentary system of government, but this is rejected by an opposition spokesman. Tentative plans are made for reform, including the provision that the President step down by year's end, but some protesters demand he step down immediately.

records.label: Yemen crisis
records.text: The government deploys military vehicles and extra troops in Sana'a.
